chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “A deceased person dies while in a state of janabah; how is he to be washed, and how much water suffices for him?” He said: “He is to be given one ghusl, and that suffices for janabah and for the ghusl of the deceased, because they are two sanctities that have come together in one single sanctity.”

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: major ritual impurity caused by janabah
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: he is to be washed ritually

ai.seo_question: How should a deceased person who died in a state of janabah be washed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a deceased person who died in a state of janabah. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that one ghusl is sufficient for both janabah and the washing of the deceased, since the two sanctities are combined into one.
